items.title: What falling home prices mean for affordability
items.description: Australian house prices have recorded their biggest monthly fall since 2022. For young buyers hoping it's a turning point, economists have some bad news.

items.title: US launches strikes as Iran says Strait of Hormuz is closed
items.description: Iran earlier said it considered the Strait of Hormuz closed once again after a vessel used an "unauthorised route" through the strait, prompting the Revolutionary Guard to fire on the vessel.

items.title: Man charged with the murder of missing mum after body found
items.description: A 48-year-old man has been charged with murder after the body of missing mother Jana Armstrong was found in bushland late on Saturday.

items.title: Israeli court battle threatens to turn into constitutional crisis
items.description: A Trumpian clash between the Netanyahu government and Israel's most senior court is rapidly building into a major constitutional crisis.

items.title: The perils of a holiday when you're in a leadership position
items.description: For Australian politicians, Scott Morrison's ill-fated Hawaii vacation in December 2019 remains a potent reminder of what not to do in a national crisis.

items.title: Live: Messi assists early Argentina strike against Switzerland in quarterfinal
items.description: Lionel Messi looks to lead Argentina to yet another World Cup semifinal as they take on Switzerland in Kansas City. Follow live.

items.title: Risks and rewards of playing diplomatic football in the Pacific
items.description: In a contest for Pacific influence against China, Australia's football diplomacy comes with risks and rewards.

items.title: UK police arrest 28-year-old man in Ann Widdecombe murder case
items.description: Police previously arrested, then later released, a 26-year-old man in relation to the alleged murder, after Ann Widdecombe's body was found in her residence on Thursday.

items.title: As Japan's population shrinks, 'urban bears' are moving in
items.description: When Araki Osamu first heard reports a bear had been seen in the streets of his home town, a 1-hour bullet train ride north of Tokyo, he dismissed it as "fake news".

items.title: Two religions, one friendship group and a whole lot of kindness
items.description: When a group of Jewish mates decided to support a newly arrived Muslim family, all of their lives would change. Together they have flipped expectations about religion and friendship.

items.title: Theoretical 'mirror life' could grow out of control, scientists fear
items.description: This year, scientists included a new potential threat in their decision to move the Doomsday Clock closer to midnight. So what is 'mirror life' and why are they concerned?

items.title: Owner taken to court over $1m damage bill to 110yo cafe
items.description: The heritage-listed former Paragon Cafe in Katoomba was once considered a success story of Greek entrepreneurship, but has now landed in the NSW Land and Envicronment Court.

items.title: Young country footballer 'alert' after serious on-field head knock
items.description: A young regional footballer who sustained a head knock and concussion during a match on Saturday is recovering well in a Melbourne hospital, according to his club.

items.title: Nosková downs 'ex-friend' Muchová to win all-Czech Wimbledon final
items.description: Linda Nosková becomes the third Czech woman in four years to claim the Wimbledon singles title as she downs her great friend in the final.

items.title: From Heath Ledger protégé to abuse survivor, Grace Woodroofe perseveres
items.description: Heath Ledger launched her music career at just 17, but an emotionally abusive relationship with a fellow musician derailed it. A decade on, Grace Woodroofe is releasing the soundtrack to her survival.

items.title: How WWI helped shape what you call this deli meat
items.description: The words we use for a handful of classic Australian foods can tell a lot about where we come from.

items.title: The Invite welcomes you to one of the best films of 2026
items.description: Olivia Wilde's return to directing might take place almost entirely in a single room, but it unfolds all the relationship anxieties we prefer to keep hidden at home.

items.title: New images offer rare glimpse into Shackleton's landmark Antarctic expedition

items.title: Typhoon makes landfall in China as millions of people take shelter
items.description: Typhoon Bavi brings strong winds and heavy rain as it makes landfall in Zhejiang province in eastern China.

items.title: Artist fighting Temu to reclaim her mosaic design
items.description: A South Australian artist is fighting drop-ship company Temu over its selling of her mosaic design on rugs. But how did the artwork get there in the first place?

items.title: Can Australia avoid the next round of the global energy crisis?
items.description: As the conflict has dragged on, gas prices have soared and now threaten to up-end the economies of Europe and Asia.

items.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill seven, wound dozens more
items.description: Five of the people were killed when two glide bombs hit a crowded area in the northern city of ​Sumy, a frequent Russian target.

items.title: Skier training for 2030 Winter Paralympics only a year after discovering sport
items.description: Oliberth Reyes has moved to the Snowy Mountains to train to qualify for the 2030 Winter Paralympics despite learning to ski only a year ago.

items.title: The 100-million-year-old cold case and the aquatic dinosaur called Moria
items.description: Travis Enright is four months into investigating what he calls "a 100-million-year-old cold case" involving a 10-metre-long aquatic dinosaur called Moria.

items.title: Numbat population improves amid warning there is a long way to go
items.description: Numbats, Western Australia's animal emblem, have been pulled from the brink of extinction after research found the population was growing in the wild.
